sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 3 = check 2; Internal Quality Checks row 3, no annotation text for this row; Deterministic Checks row 13 check-instruction-content.py: 'Voice and grammar are left to the rubric')
evidence: instruction.md itself meets the row. It is 3 short paragraphs (683 bytes), first person, with a contraction and personal habit detail: instruction.md:1 "I'd like a small local playground ... I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source."; instruction.md:5 "I should be able to open it, edit code, run it and inspect the result without signing in." Sentence lengths vary (8 to 31 words), there are no bullets, no headings, no parallel lists and no marketing gloss; a grep of instruction.md and all six notes for seamless/robust/delve/comprehensive/leverage/ensure and em dashes returned nothing. The template instruction.md is the single CHANGE_ME line, so the wording is task-authored and in scope. Residual, real but bounded: the skill reference (quality-checks.md:15) also lists as a defect 'a voice that changes between instruction.md and the notes', and its Verify line expects 'contractions, the occasional terse fragment in the notes'. The six notes (1647 words) contain zero contractions (the only apostrophes are possessives: behaviour.md:9 "snippet's", security.md:3 "app's") and no terse fragments; they are written almost entirely as uniform imperative/modal specification, e.g. behaviour.md:13 "History inspection is read-only. Restoring an older snapshot creates a new current revision of the same record while retaining the intervening history.", integration.md:11 "Symbolic links are unsupported except links under /app/node_modules whose resolved targets also stay under /app/node_modules.", security.md:5 "Refuse dynamic evaluation through eval, Function, WebAssembly, new workers and dynamic module imports with clear feedback." The requester's first person survives only in a few places (overview.md:3 "while I work"; ui.md:3 "the source I see"; behaviour.md:11 "That refresh must not touch what I am doing ... keep my draft; do not load the newer revision over my work"; integration.md:3 "We start it with"), and policy.md and security.md have none. So the register moves from a casual personal ask to a formal contract. I judge this not a blocking defect: the notes are plain, concrete, unpadded, vary in sentence length, use the same British spelling throughout (behaviour, colour) and the precision is needed by the strict contract; nothing reads as marketing or templated LLM filler. No runtime measurement applies to this row. risk=true only because a hosted source reviewer applying quality-checks.md:15 literally could flag the notes register; I cannot predict that outcome.
suggested_fix: Optional, wording only and without changing any requirement: carry the requester's voice into the notes that currently have none, for example a first-person line and a contraction or two in policy.md, security.md and behaviour.md:13 ("I only want to look at history, not edit it"; "don't load the newer revision over my work" at behaviour.md:11). Any such edit changes the input bytes and invalidates this clearance.
